findings.title: Message bundles are read with PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream), which is not UTF-8
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() constructs PropertyResourceBundle from a FileInputStream for the target file at line 68 and for the English reference file at line 77. PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream) loads properties as ISO-8859-1, while Keycloak theme message files are UTF-8 and contain non-ASCII translated text. The verifier therefore compares mojibake for many translations, making the HTML check unreliable and likely to produce false positives or false negatives. Use PropertyResourceBundle(Reader) with an InputStreamReader using StandardCharsets.UTF_8.

findings.title: Unescaping sanitizer output can hide sanitization changes
findings.body: After the OWASP sanitizer produces output, the code unescapes HTML entities with StringEscapeUtils.unescapeHtml4() before comparing the sanitized value to the original value. If the sanitizer neutralizes markup by escaping it, this conversion can restore the original markup representation and make the two strings compare equal. That can hide cases where sanitization actually changed the value, so the verifier may accept HTML that was not truly unchanged/safe.

findings.title: Anchor regex matches tags that are not anchors
findings.body:
ANCHOR_PATTERN is defined as ]*>, which matches any tag whose name begins with the letter a, such as ,
, or , not just and . santizeAnchors() removes matching tags before the OWASP allow-list is applied. If such a tag appears in both the English and translated value, it can bypass the intended HTML policy even though only anchor tags were meant to be treated specially. The pattern should match only anchor tags.

findings.title: English reference file is derived with fragile path rewriting
findings.body: The verifier locates the English bundle by rewriting the absolute file path: replacing resources-community with resources and then applying a locale-suffix regex to the whole path. This assumes every verified file has a locale suffix matching that regex and that an English file exists at the rewritten path. Files without the expected suffix, locale-like path elements elsewhere in the path, or community-only messages can resolve to the wrong file or cause a RuntimeException instead of a normal verification message. This makes the verifier brittle and can fail builds for reasons unrelated to HTML safety.

findings.title: Difference reporting can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException
findings.body: When reporting a sanitization mismatch, the code computes a common prefix and a common suffix independently, then calls substring(start, length - end) without ensuring that the prefix and suffix do not overlap. If one string is an extension of the other at the beginning or end, start can become greater than length - end, causing String.substring to throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The verifier should clamp or otherwise handle overlapping prefix/suffix ranges before creating the diagnostic substrings.

findings.title: templateHelp whitelist removes arbitrary uppercase tags before sanitization
findings.body: normalizeValue() removes substrings matching CLAIM.<uppercase letters> before HTML sanitization. This is broader than the intended CLAIM.<NAME> placeholder and can hide uppercase HTML-style tags prefixed with CLAIM. from the sanitizer check, while the actual resource value still contains them. Whitelist only the exact expected placeholder, or normalize it in a way that does not silently remove arbitrary tag-like content.

findings.title: Account UI message changed from i18next placeholders to Java MessageFormat
findings.body: The account-ui bundle uses i18next-style interpolation elsewhere, such as {{date}} and {{0}}. Changing error-invalid-multivalued-size to Java MessageFormat placeholders and a choice subformat means the JS UI will not interpolate this message correctly; users are likely to see literal {0}/{2,choice,...} text or an incorrectly formatted message. If pluralization is needed in the UI, use the UI's i18n plural mechanism rather than Java MessageFormat.

findings.title: Admin UI message changed from i18next placeholders to Java MessageFormat
findings.body: This admin-ui bundle previously used i18next-style double-curly placeholders for this key. Replacing {{0}}, {{1}}, and {{2}} with Java MessageFormat placeholders and a choice subformat is inconsistent with the JS i18n format and can break interpolation in the admin UI. The message will likely render with literal placeholder text or fail to pluralize correctly.

findings.title: Lithuanian account translation contains Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian account message totpStep1 is set to the Italian sentence Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:. This is not Lithuanian and will be shown to Lithuanian users.

findings.title: Lithuanian login translation contains Italian text
findings.body: The Lithuanian login message loginTotpStep1 is set to the Italian sentence Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:. This is not Lithuanian and will be shown to Lithuanian users.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese locale uses Traditional Chinese text
findings.body: The zh_CN account message totpStep1 uses Traditional Chinese characters in a Simplified Chinese locale. The string should be localized using Simplified Chinese characters consistent with zh_CN.

findings.title: Tests do not cover UTF-8/non-ASCII message bundles
findings.body: The added tests use only ASCII fixtures and do not exercise real-world UTF-8 translated message files. Because the implementation reads property bundles in a way that is sensitive to character encoding, the current tests cannot catch encoding-related false positives or false negatives. Add fixtures containing non-ASCII UTF-8 characters, HTML, and locale-specific path/name patterns.
